title: SIEM export connector resilience and event contract spec
content:
Purpose:
This spec defines the resilience model, event-level contract, transformation guidance, and customer onboarding checklist for Redwood's SIEM export connectors (Splunk HTTP Event Collector, Datadog Logs API, Azure Sentinel/Log Analytics). It focuses on robust delivery semantics, schema compatibility, privacy/redaction, and operational observability so connector behavior is predictable across customer environments.

Scope and goals:
- Supported endpoints: Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs ingest, Azure Sentinel (Log Analytics Data Collector API).
- Primary goals: ensure at-least-once delivery under transient failures, avoid amplification/backpressure on Redwood serving runtime, provide clear mapping to downstream SIEM schemas, and give customers a checklist for field restrictions and PII handling.
- Not in scope: deep storage archival policies (handled by separate archival spec), SIEM-side parse rules.

High-level assumptions:
- Downstream SIEMs accept JSON or ndjson payloads over HTTPS; auth is token-based (HEC token, Datadog API key, Azure shared key).
- Customers may enforce strict schemas or parsers; connectors must offer transformation modes: passthrough, normalize, and strict-contract.

Event contract (canonical Redwood export event):
- Each exported record must include top-level fields (lowercase):
  - timestamp: RFC3339 UTC string
  - tenant_id: string (customer org id)
  - route_id: string (Redwood API route or workload identifier)
  - event_type: string (audit|access|inference|system|error)
  - request_id: string (UUID correlate across logs/traces)
  - model: string (model id/version)
content_continued:
- tokens_generated: integer (optional)
  - latency_ms: integer (end-to-end ms)
  - outcome: string (success|failure|fallback)
  - payload: string (short string or redacted prompt summary)
  - meta: string (optional JSON string for downstream-only fields)

Note: JSON fields must be string or number types; avoid nested objects except 'meta' which is a stringified JSON to simplify SIEM ingestion.

SIEM-specific mapping guidance (examples):
- Splunk HEC (raw event mode): send each canonical event as a single JSON object per line. Recommended field mapping: Splunk _time <- timestamp, tenant_id -> tenant_id, sourcetype -> redwood:llm:event, host -> route_id, _raw -> full JSON. For customers using Splunk props/transforms, supply sample props.conf to extract tokens_generated and outcome.
- Datadog Logs API: send JSON log with attributes: timestamp (epoch ms), dd.service = "redwood-inference", dd.source = "llm-export", dd.tags = "tenant:{tenant_id},route:{route_id},model:{model}". Place canonical JSON in the message attribute.
- Azure Sentinel / Log Analytics: map to Common Schema where possible. recommended CustomLog name: RedwoodLLMCL. Map timestamp -> TimeGenerated, tenant_id -> TenantId_s, model -> Model_s, outcome -> Outcome_s, tokens_generated -> TokensGenerated_d. Provide a sample ingestion rule for customers who use Azure sentinel parsers.

Transformation modes (connector config):
- passthrough: emit Redwood raw audit/log object with minimal changes (fastest, largest payload).
- normalize: apply canonical event contract, drop nested objects, ensure limited payload size, perform standard redaction.
- strict-contract: validate against schema and reject non-conforming events (useful for customers with strict parsers).

Backpressure and retry semantics (resilience model):
- Delivery semantics: connectors implement at-least-once delivery using an internal durable queue (in-memory with spill-to-disk fallback).
- Retry policy: transient errors (5xx, network) -> exponential backoff with jitter: initial=250ms, multiplier=2, max_interval=30s, max_attempts=8.
- Throttling: if downstream returns 429 or 503 with Retry-After, respect Retry-After for that token and apply per-tenant backoff window. Avoid global slowdowns; per-tenant and per-destination rate limits.
- Queue bounds: default in-memory queue per-tenant: 5k events or 8MB, then spill to disk up to 1M events or 2GB. When disk threshold reached, connector enters shedding mode: prioritize control-plane health and drop lowest-priority telemetry (system debug), while marking dropped events in an internal summary metric.
- Idempotency: include an idempotency_key = request_id + sha256(payload) for events to allow downstream dedup if supported.

Batching and payload limits:
- Default batch window: 250ms or 200 events, whichever first.
- Max batch size: 1MB for Splunk HEC (per Splunk recommendation), 5MB for Datadog, 1MB for Azure Log Analytics.
- Large items: if a single event > max_payload, apply inline truncation rules (keep header fields, truncate payload to 2k chars) and add field truncated = true and truncated_bytes integer.

Privacy and PII handling:
- Default redaction rules: remove sequences matching email, SSN, credit card numbers by regex. Replace with token <REDACTED_EMAIL> etc.
- Sensitive field map: customers can supply allowlist/denylist for additional keys that should be stripped at export time.
- Evidence automation: connector can optionally attach an "evidence_reference" pointing to Redwood private evidence store (S3/GCS) rather than including raw prompt; evidence_reference format: s3://redwood-evidence/{tenant_id}/{date}/{uuid}.

Observability and metrics (what connector must emit):
- per-tenant metrics (time-series): exported_events_total, exported_events_failed_total, exported_events_dropped_total, exported_events_retried_total, current_queue_depth, current_disk_spill_bytes, last_success_timestamp.
- tracing: instrument each export attempt with trace id = request_id; include span for transform->send->ack.
- logging: structured logs for connector state transitions (entering_spill_mode, resuming_normal, drop_summary). Logs must include tenant_id and route_id.

Customer onboarding checklist (minimum required from customer):
- Endpoint URL and token (HEC token / Datadog API key / Azure workspace id + key).
- Allowed source IP ranges (if customer require IP allowlisting) -- provide list of Redwood egress ranges.
- Required field mappings or strict schema: if customer uses strict-contract mode, they must provide sample events and a schema/props to validate against.
- Redaction policy: provide allowlist/denylist or accept Redwood default.
- Expected volume: average logs/sec and burst QPS for capacity planning.
- SLA tier: hosted vs dedicated affects connector throughput and retention; document which tier applies.

Validation and integration tests:
- Unit tests for transform rules (regex redaction, field renames, truncation).
- Integration tests: local harness that fakes endpoints and asserts correct HTTP status handling, honoring Retry-After, idempotency header, and batch sizes.
- Load test: simulate 10x expected burst for at least 5 minutes and assert queue spill behavior and shedding mode thresholds.

Operational playbooks (incident examples):
- Downstream 5xx spike: connector should backoff per-tenant and emit alert when exported_events_failed_total > 5% over 1m window. Runbook: investigate downstream health, apply temporary rate-limit per-tenant, notify customer of degraded export.
- Disk-spill saturation: alarm when current_disk_spill_bytes > 75% of threshold; runbook: triage backlog, increase retention or escalate to infra to increase available disk.

Sample props (Splunk) and ingestion rule snippets (to supply to customers):
- props.conf suggestion:
  [redwood:llm:event]
  TZ = UTC
  SHOULD_LINEMERGE = false
  KV_MODE = json

- Azure custom log example mapping (Kusto):
  RedwoodLLMCL
  | extend TimeGenerated = todatetime(TimeGenerated), TenantId_s, Model_s, Outcome_s

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we support exactly-once semantics for dedicated customers with persistent stores? (follow-up: design for checkpointed durable queue with transactional delivery).
- Customer preference for nested JSON vs flattened fields (some SIEMs prefer flattened). We'll add per-customer flattening transform as config.

Appendix: sample event (normalized mode):
{
  "timestamp": "2025-08-01T14:22:03Z",
  "tenant_id": "org_abc123",
  "route_id": "prod-search-1",
  "event_type": "inference",
  "request_id": "c3f9b2ea-4b9a-4a7e-9f77-e2d1f0a13b9f",
  "model": "redwood/llm-large:2025-06-12",
  "tokens_generated": 78,
  "latency_ms": 245,
  "outcome": "success",
  "payload": "<REDACTED_PROMPT_SUMMARY>",
  "meta": "{\"client_region\":\"us-west-2\"}"
}

Notes on uniqueness: this doc emphasizes resilience (queue spill, disk fallback, shedding), explicit per-tenant backoff, idempotency_key usage, and evidence_reference pattern which is not present in other SIEM export docs.

Next steps:
- Engineering: implement durable queue + spill behavior prototype (eng infra ticket JIRA-SEC-789).
- Product: finalize default redaction regex list and evidence store retention policy.
- Security: review idempotency_key hashing for potential information leakage.

Contact: Avery Chen (a.chen@redwood.com) for questions and to schedule integration runbook review.
